title: The $7 Coffee That Could Cost You $50,000
segments: That seven-dollar coffee isn't the problem. The habit behind it might be.
Picture buying one coffee every weekday. Seven dollars, five days a week, fifty weeks a year. That's seventeen hundred and fifty dollars a year.
Now imagine investing that same amount instead, every year, for fifteen years.

At a hypothetical seven percent annual return, compounded weekly, you'd end up with roughly forty-four thousand dollars. Your own contributions would be twenty-six thousand two hundred and fifty. The rest would be investment growth.
But here's the catch: seven percent is an assumption, not a guarantee. Markets go down too. Fees, taxes, and inflation matter.
The point isn't to quit coffee. It's to notice the small repeat expenses you don't actually value.
Pick one. Redirect that money toward a goal you care about. Follow The Money Stickman for money lessons that make sense.
